sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: European wild ginger is a low, creeping evergreen perennial, usually about 5–10 cm tall, with glossy kidney-shaped leaves. Its small dark purplish flowers sit close to the ground beneath the foliage. It is native from Europe east to central Siberia and favours shaded woodland.

sections.title: Safety and image
sections.text: The plant is listed as toxic if ingested; no safe food use was verified. Research has reported aristolochic-acid-related compounds in Asarum and an intoxication case involving A. europaeum, but this does not establish a dose for each plant part. The plate's hidden flowers and rounded leaves match its growth form.
